unharnessed.meaning: Every point survives, from the compliance burden to the API use case; nothing added.
unharnessed.sense: Mostly exact ("knock up a website", "grunt work", "weak spots", "dead easy"). "get the tick-off on content updates" strains: the idiom is "get the tick", and "tick-off" can read as a telling-off.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural, low-key Australian office voice: "chances are you've been handed what looks like a simple job", "Static websites have a few things going for them".
unharnessed.register: Retold throughout but on the light side of level 3; a handful of terms ("knock up", "grunt work", "dead easy") over plain casual English. No swearing, allowed under vulgarity 1.
unharnessed.tone: Keeps the friendly, persuasive product tone.
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly; "Steering clear of a traditional CMS means steering clear of headaches" is a deliberate echo that works.
unharnessed.variety: Reasonably varied, without leaning on any term.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the cloud.gov Pages pitch, with its headings, bullets and diagram link intact.

engine.meaning: Mostly the original verbatim, but "a seemingly simple bloody hard yakka" contradicts itself (a simple task called hard work), and "ya old bastard" adds an insult to the reader.
engine.sense: "hard yakka" replaces "task" as if it were a noun for a job, which it is not, and contradicts "seemingly simple".
engine.authenticity: Swears bolted on: "bloody hard yakka", "ya old bastard"; "properly easy" is a British form.
engine.register: Almost entirely untranslated; the few changes are a swear and an insult. "bastard" is within vulgarity 1 but the level is far below 3.
engine.tone: "ya old bastard" turns a polite government product page into an insult to its reader.
engine.flow: "a seemingly simple bloody hard yakka: create a website" breaks the grammar.
engine.essence: Recognisably the original, because it is the original.

yarn.meaning: Every point survives. "already flat-out web team" elaborates "extra strain"; "the tick from the higher-ups" narrows "stakeholders", who are not necessarily superiors.
yarn.sense: Terms fit: "the real hard yakka", "knock up a website", "babysitting server applications", "fewer holes in it". "higher-ups" for stakeholders is slightly narrower.
yarn.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian colleague explaining it: "Thing is, the real hard yakka usually isn't writing the content", "plus all the database scaling and backup carry-on".
yarn.register: Right weight for level 3: steady, natural Aussie through every section, without becoming a yarn. No swearing, allowed under vulgarity 1.
yarn.tone: Keeps the friendly, persuasive product tone.
yarn.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "So the whole site's easier to look after and has fewer holes in it."
yarn.variety: Varied: "dead simple", "hard yakka", "flat-out", "babysitting", "carry-on", "have a go at", "lumps you with". "dead" appears twice.
